assertions.name: colour_tube_refinement_cannot_reach_required_trace
assertions.source: max_b tr_M(beta_b) / sqrt(B_AME); < 1 means unreachable by any convex reweighting, per QOU.MassTheory.convex_comb_le_bound

assertions.name: control_branch_count_unchanged
assertions.source: the refinement reweights arcs; it adds no strands

assertions.name: control_branches_spread_above_the_atom
assertions.source: max_b / tr_M(atom); > 1, so the bound is not trivially satisfied

assertions.name: block_states_its_weights_are_nonneg_and_normalised
assertions.source: grep of inter-nucleon-channel-color-tube.md for 'W in Q_{>=0}' and 'normalised to sum W = 1'

description: conj:inter-nucleon-channel-color-tube fixes W >= 0 normalised to sum W = 1, so the refined atom is a REWEIGHTING of the same 32 branches, not a new element. QOU.MassTheory.convex_comb_le_bound then bounds it by max_b tr_M = 1.018275 against a required 1.491498 -- unreachable, ratio 0.68272. The refinement cannot supply the deuteron binding MAGNITUDE. Scope (b); the escape is a larger index set, i.e. a satellite/cabling move (larger_index_set_escapes_the_bound).
caveats: SCOPE (b): the invariant is branch convexity (measured in atom-branch-convexity-bound) plus convex_comb_le_bound (Lean, sorry-free). It bounds the MAGNITUDE only. It does NOT say the colour-tube refinement is wrong -- the p/n asymmetry and chirality sign structure it exists for are untouched.

The escape is a LARGER INDEX SET, exhibited in Lean by larger_index_set_escapes_the_bound: a satellite/cabling move puts the branches in a bigger algebra, outside the hypotheses. NOT claimed that such a construction DOES reach the target -- only that this theorem does not forbid it.
ONE isotope (deuteron), and the underlying max_b comes through binding_k_solver.per_block_evaluation, which is float64. The verdict turns on a 47 % gap, far above that resolution.
